coverageNote.note: NFI operates 300+ North American facilities; we audited 10 of the largest and most yard-intensive (dedicated DCs, port logistics, a Port of Savannah terminal, a fulfillment center). The rest follow the same gate/dock archetypes.

account.dossierIntro: NFI runs freight yards on behalf of the retailers and manufacturers it serves, across more than 300 North American facilities. We mapped 10 of its largest and most yard-intensive sites, from Lehigh Valley cross-docks to Inland Empire import DCs and a Port of Savannah logistics terminal, holding 1,363 dock doors and room for about 3,205 trailers. Control across the network is uneven. Six of the 10 sit behind a truck gate, but only 3 run a staffed booth, and several sit open to the road. YardFlow puts one gate-to-dock standard across every yard NFI operates, no matter whose freight is moving through it.
surprisingFindings: Only 6 of NFI’s 10 audited yards sit behind a truck gate, and 3 run a staffed booth. The rest sit open to the road, so most trailers roll in unchecked.
The 10 yards hold 1,363 dock doors and room for about 3,205 trailers, and not one is rail-served. Every load moves by truck.
Ten sites span four yard types, from a Port of Savannah terminal to Inland Empire DCs and Lehigh Valley cross-docks, each with its own gate routine.

sites.name: NFI Distribution Center Breinigsville PA

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coordinates (40.567597, -75.636086) landed on the south wall of a
long white-roofed industrial building inside a dense Lehigh Valley industrial
park (Breinigsville / Upper Macungie Twp). Web research confirms 200 Nestle Way
is an NFI Industries distribution center: 384,500 SF, built 2021, 36 ft clear,
off I-78 Exit 49 (NFI facility profile PDF; LoopNet; bippermedia listing).

Positive building ID was clinched in Street View: looking west into the truck
entrance off Nestle Way (pano `eK1Ypep7U5qFhimzTfVzJw`, panos along the road),
the building face carries the blue "NFI" logo and NFI-blue accent panels.
The same blue/white NFI building is seen from the south perimeter road (pano
`8e6EvxSowR8LTYuOqkemJw`). This is the correct building, not an office or
neighbor. Locked center ~40.56790, -75.63500.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Single divided truck entrance off Nestle Way at the SE corner. z21 satellite shows two yellow/black striped barrier arms, one across the inbound lane and one across the outbound lane, separated by a landscaped median. Confirmed in Street View (pano eK1Ypep7U5qFhimzTfVzJw, 2025-05).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth visible at the gate from satellite or Street View. The barrier arms appear automated with a kiosk/call-box; no 1-3-space guard structure beside the lane. Hence remoteGs = true.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present, no guard shack -> remote/automated check-in (kiosk/app).
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Set false / entryExitSeparate false because the gate is a single divided in/out point at one location rather than two distinct gates at different property points; in and out share the same entrance throat with split lanes (1 in, 1 out).

fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved apron between the gate arms and the north dock face provides interior queue/holding room before docks.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Single continuous dock face along the building's NORTH side (~700ft) with a regular door rhythm and trailers backed in across z19/z20 crops; comfortably in the 50+ band. Count ~70 is an overhead estimate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Three diagonal trailer-parking rows in the north/east yard hold parked trailers without tractors; 25-50 band.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Main dock bank on the north face plus a separate angled dock/trailer cluster on the building's EAST end (eastend-z19) suggests physically separate dock clusters; medium confidence.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated diagonal trailer-storage rows separate from active dock staging, in the north and east yard.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town Lehigh Valley industrial park surrounded by farmland, woods, a stormwater pond, and a residential subdivision to the south; broader setting is Rural per the tie-break rule.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Estimate of diagonal-stall capacity across the three drop rows plus dock apron; overhead approximation.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Derived from the perimeter polygon (~22.5 acres inside the fence line).

sites.name: NFI Distribution Center Florence NJ
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coordinates (40.11814, -74.80977) were wrong. A z16 satellite probe
there showed a residential neighborhood with municipal ball fields in central
Florence Township — no industrial building. The real facility is **NFI Park at
Florence Crossings**, an NFI-developed multi-tenant logistics campus at
2020 US-130 North, "less than half a mile from NJ Turnpike Exit 6A," about
1.5 km SSW of the bad pin (NFI Industries and Florence Township sources).

Working SW from the bad point, a z15 probe at 40.105, -74.825 surfaced the campus:
a cluster of large distribution buildings between the Delaware River and US-130 /
the NJ Turnpike. The campus comprises ~1.65M SF across four tenant buildings
(Subaru parts DC, QPSI, and others). The audited building is the **Subaru of
America parts distribution + training center** that NFI built-to-suit here:

fieldNotes.truckGate: Open business-park campus (NFI Park at Florence Crossings). No barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint anywhere along the internal access road (Crossings Blvd) or at the building's truck court. Street View on the south loop road and satellite of every access point confirm open driveways from public road to docks.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at any entrance. No 1-3-space structure beside any drive. Confirmed in Street View (open landscaped frontage) and satellite.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide shared truck court between the Subaru/NFI building and the adjacent DC; trailers staged along a central landscaped median inside the property.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Truck court / dock-approach aisle is deep and wide, easily holding 3+ trucks in queue.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Subaru/NFI build-to-suit spec is 83 loading doors (NFI/Florence Township sources); satellite shows a long bank of doors with trailers backed in along the west face plus additional doors at the north end. Banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large dedicated trailer drop yard at the NW of the parcel plus heavy trailer staging through the court; well over 50 drop trailers visible without tractors.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Audited building is one tenant building within the 4-building, ~1.65M SF NFI Park at Florence Crossings campus (Subaru, QPSI, and others share the property).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Planned logistics park on the edge of Florence Township (a small town) beside US-130 and NJ Turnpike Exit 6A, with farmland/open land and residential adjacent. Per rubric (small-town industrial -> Rural). Listed uncertain given the heavy surrounding logistics development.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: No gate present, so no controlled inbound lane count; the internal road and court are open 2-way pavement.
fieldNotes.exitLanes: No gate present, so no controlled outbound lane count.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Estimated from the perimeter polygon enclosing the audited Subaru/NFI building, its west truck court, north drop yard, and south office parking (~44 ac from the polygon); the full multi-tenant park is larger.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Approximate count of trailers in captured imagery (docks + drop yard + court staging).
fieldNotes.streetViewMeta: Only Street View coverage on the parcel is pano iA_Q0KZKtWn73NgJAiliHw on the southern internal loop road (2022-10), used for the perimeter view (camera heading 346 toward the building south end). No pano within 300m of the north truck court, so truckGate has no coverage.

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coordinates (32.15001, -81.151175) landed squarely on the site. I
probed satellite at z15–z19 around the point and cross-checked the street
address and NFI's published material. The cross/T-shaped warehouse footprint in
the imagery matches NFI's Savannah transload building, and web research
confirms the address and specs. Positively identified.

The site sits on a peninsula formed by a bend in the Savannah River (bounding
it on the north and east), with a residential neighborhood (Crossgate) and a
rail/utility corridor to the west, and Crossgate Road along the south/SE.
NFI states the facility is less than 1 mile from the GPA Garden City Terminal
— consistent with the location.

---

fieldNotes.imagery: Static Maxar satellite available via probe.ts captures the site MID-CONSTRUCTION (bare graded dirt, partially-erected steel/precast warehouse roofs, stacked construction materials, no final pavement striping). The facility opened Dec 5 2023; current imagery predates completion. Street View near the entrance is dated 2019-05 and shows raw, fenced vacant land (no operational coverage). Location, building footprint and graded property boundary are positively confirmed; gate-detail fields are inferred from facility type + documented specs and flagged.
fieldNotes.location: Positively confirmed as 120 Crossgate Road, Port Wentworth GA. The cross/T-shaped warehouse footprint in the imagery matches NFI's transload building; site sits on a peninsula bounded by the Savannah River (N/E) and the residential Crossgate neighborhood (W), <1 mi from GPA Garden City Terminal.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 308 shipping doors per NFI's published facility specs (counted as 50+ band). Two long dock faces visible on the building's main E-W bar and its N-S wing.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Two distinct dock banks on different building faces (main bar south face + perpendicular wing), consistent with separate inbound/outbound transload flows.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 876 trailer spots per published specs plus 9,500-TEU container stacking; large graded drop-yard areas flank the building N and NE (50+ band). dropYard: true.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Inferred true: secured port transload container yard (9,500 TEU) is fenced (2019 SV shows full perimeter chain-link) with a single controlled access from the SE off Crossgate Road; small structures cluster at the SE corner of the truck court. Barrier arm not directly visible in construction imagery.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true: small structure cluster at the SE corner of the truck court (~32.1483,-81.1518) is consistent with a gatehouse/check-in; a manned booth is near-certain for a bonded/secured port container yard. Not directly confirmable in construction imagery.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs NW-SE along the western edge by the neighborhood but appears to be a through-line, not a spur into the property. railServed: false (drayage/transload by truck from the port terminal).
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated 2 in / 1 out from the wide access apron at the SE entrance; exact lane count not confirmable in construction imagery.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved gate apron and very large yard footprint leave ample room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town industrial peninsula adjacent to a small residential neighborhood and the port; not dense metro fabric -> Rural per rubric tie-break.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: 0 trailers visible because imagery predates operations (site under construction).

The site access drive connects openly to the internal commerce-park parkway (Logistics Pkwy). fieldNotes.guardShack: No 1-3-stall guard booth visible at the entrance throat or anywhere on the truck path (z19/z20). The only structures are the main building and a small electrical/utility enclosure. Called false.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because truckGate is false (no gate present to be remotely controlled).

fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Approach from the parkway into the NE-end court easily holds 3+ trucks before the dock line.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single access drive off the parkway at the NE end serves both in and out.

fieldNotes.dockDoors: JLL/sale listings state 102 dock levelers; doors counted on both long faces in imagery are consistent (>50).
fieldNotes.dropArea: 270 trailer parking spaces (expandable to 307) per JLL; drop trailers visible in the NW drop yard and along courts. 50+ band.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Cross-dock: dock banks on both opposite long faces (NE and SW), enabling separate ship/receive operations.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Old Augusta Commerce Center, Rincon/Effingham County edge of Savannah metro, surrounded by pine forest and undeveloped parcels; Street View shows a rural two-lane road. Rural.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Rural but inside an active master-planned commerce park near I-95/Hwy 21 corridor; carrier coverage likely adequate. Low-confidence call of false.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage area in the broad paved/graded expanse NW of the building between the NFI building and the adjacent DC, plus drop rows along the courts.
